name: Botox wearing off after two months
summary:
**Conversation Overview**

The person asked a question about whether it is normal for the effects of a cosmetic injectable treatment to wear off quickly, approximately one month after a follow-up appointment. They noted they had an initial appointment followed by a two-week follow-up that required additional injections, and expressed that the results felt short-lived relative to the financial investment. They spoke positively about their provider and were not attributing the outcome to any error on the provider's part.

Claude explained that faster-than-expected results wearing off is common for first-time recipients, as the muscles are not yet conditioned to relax, and noted that some individuals metabolize the treatment more quickly due to individual variation. Claude advised that longevity typically improves with consistent subsequent treatments and recommended the person discuss their experience with their provider so dosage notes can be adjusted for future appointments.

chat_messages.text: Answer this question. Were they short comment: I got botox for the 1st time on March 6 and had a 2 week follow up on March 20. She had to do more injections on my follow. I am now a month out from that appointment and I feel like my botox is completely wearing off. Is that normal? 😬 I absolutely love the provider and I know it isnt her fault. I just feel like that was alot of money for not even 2 months.

chat_messages.text:
This is actually pretty common, especially for first-timers. Your muscles weren't "trained" yet to relax, so first treatments often metabolize faster. Some people are also just fast metabolizers genetically.

The good news: it typically lasts longer with each subsequent treatment as the muscles learn to stay relaxed. Most providers recommend staying consistent for the first few rounds to build that up.

Worth mentioning it to your provider at your next appointment so she can note your dosage and adjust if needed. You may just need a slightly higher unit count to hold longer.
